subject: Deployment path qualification - Hosted vs Dedicated follow-up
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Jenkins <samira@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fastlane.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + data request: deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Samira / Liam,

Great to meet you this morning — thanks for walking us through FastLane's inference use cases. I wanted to capture next steps and ask for a couple data points that will let us recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Recap (very short):
- Primary product: real-time personalization API for search + recommendations.
- Peak characteristics: bursty traffic around product launches / email sends.
- Critical SLA for realtime ranking: p95 latency target in the 50–100ms range for short prompts.
- Security: standard SOC2 + some isolated data needs for telemetry (not full regulated data stores today).

Can you confirm the following numbers (rough is fine):
1) Sustained QPS during business hours (avg) and peak burst QPS (1–3 minute spikes).
2) Typical request size distribution: % of requests <=128 tokens, 128–512, >512 (approx).
3) p95 latency requirement for the product-critical path (short prompts) vs best-effort background calls.
4) Any procurement constraints (PO required, lead time, billing cadence) that would push you toward reserved capacity?

Preliminary guidance (high level):
- If sustained QPS is under ~200 with occasional single-digit-second bursts, Hosted API is likely the fastest path.
- If you have sustained hundreds of QPS (especially with tight p95 targets at ~50–100ms), Dedicated capacity is usually required to guarantee latency and isolation.
- Private/VPC typically comes up for regulated data; we can separate that from capacity choice.

Attached: pilot-cost-estimate.xlsx and a short mutual-action-plan.docx. If you can reply with the numbers above, I’ll put together a short comparison (cost, expected p95 on us-west-2, suggested pilot sizing) by EOD.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sizing on Thurs — I’ll invite Marissa from Solutions if that works.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive

Subject: Re: Quick recap + data request: deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Jonas — great meeting. See answers below inline.

> 1) Sustained QPS during business hours (avg) and peak burst QPS (1–3 minute spikes).
We run ~450 qps sustained during peak hours (US PST region). Bursts hit ~1,200 qps for up to ~3 minutes during campaign launches. Typical off-peak is ~50–80 qps.

> 2) Typical request size distribution: % of requests <=128 tokens, 128–512, >512 (approx).
~68% <=128 tokens, ~26% 128–512, ~6% >512. The >512 requests are mostly batch-style or long-form generation for monthly reports (not on the critical path).

> 3) p95 latency requirement for the product-critical path (short prompts) vs best-effort background calls.
Our goal for the ranking path is p95 <= 60ms for the short prompts (<=128 tokens). Background generation can tolerate up to 400ms p95.

> 4) Any procurement constraints (PO required, lead time, billing cadence) that would push you toward reserved capacity?
We prefer a reserved contract for budget predictability but we need a short pilot window (3–4 weeks) to validate latency before committing. PO lead time is ~4 weeks for larger contracts.

We are in AWS us-west-2 and would prefer the deployment to stay in-region. Security is important but not full regulated workload yet — isolation is attractive though.

Appreciate the attachments. Happy to do Thurs 11/24 11am PST for the sizing call.

—Samira

Subject: Re: Quick recap + data request: deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated) — recommendation and pilot proposal

Samira / Liam — thanks for the fast turnaround and the numbers. I talked to Marissa (Solutions) and Ben (Pricing) and we have a recommended path and a short pilot plan that matches your constraints.

Recommendation (short):
- Given sustained ~450 qps with 1,200 qps short bursts and a strict p95 <= 60ms on short prompts, Dedicated capacity is the right fit to guarantee latency and consistent tail behavior.
- Hosted is attractive for non-critical workloads and can be used immediately for background jobs while we stand up Dedicated resources.
- Private/VPC isn’t strictly required today; we’ll keep the option open if isolation requirements increase.

Why Dedicated here:
- Dedicated GPU pools let us pin model variants + quantization profile and limit noisy-neighbor variance during campaign spikes.
- We can configure burst capacity for the short 3-minute events so your p95 target is preserved.
- With Dedicated we can set an SLA and an escalation path — important for launches.

Pilot proposal (conservative, 4 weeks):
1) Week 0: Provision a small dedicated pool in us-west-2 sized for 450 sustained qps (suggested baseline: 4x A100-equivalent nodes — Marissa will finalize).
2) Week 1–3: Run traffic (split) with routing policy: critical ranking -> Dedicated, background -> Hosted. We'll enable prefix/KV cache and request batching tuned for your request-size mix.
3) Week 4: Review p95 for short prompts, cost vs expected, and decide on reserved commit.

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Configuration doc and runbook (playbook for scaling during launch).
- Pilot-cost-estimate.xlsx (attached) with expected monthly cost ranges for your profile.
- MAP (mutual-action-plan.docx) with acceptance criteria and procurement checkpoints.

Next steps / asks from FastLane:
- Confirm you’re good for Thurs 11/24 11am PST for sizing with Marissa.
- Approve pilot start window: target 12/1 provisioning -> pilot running 12/1–12/28. We know your PO lead time; we can start pilot under a T&Cs short-form while the PO is processed.

I’ll upload a short performance projection (p95 estimates by model size) into the drive link and ping you before the call. Ben will join the sizing call for any pricing questions.

Thanks — excited to get this validated quickly.

Jonas Weber
